transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Silverline CISO), Aisha Rahman (Silverline SecEng), Tom Brooks (Silverline DevOps)

Summary (auto): Pen test results review focusing on high/critical vulnerabilities, discussion of remediation prioritization, secure SDLC and patch cadence, and options for Dedicated/private deployments and audit evidence. Action items captured; follow-up scheduled.

Topics: pen test findings, CVE prioritization, remediation guidance, patch cadence, secure SDLC, RBAC/SSO concerns, KMS/encryption, audit logs, SOC2/ISO evidence, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Marcus, Aisha, Tom — thanks for making time. We're here to walk through the pen test results and talk remediation and patch cadence. Priya, want to intro?
[00:12] Priya Shah: Yeah hi, I'm Priya, I'm the SE on the account. I'll run through the high-level findings and then we can dig into the specific CVEs. I pulled the summary from the pen test you'll see in the link Jordan shared earlier.
[00:25] Marcus Lee: Thanks. Quick ask — we care most about high/critical that affect our production tokenization service and anything that touches customer PII. Also need to confirm audit log fidelity for forensics.
[00:39] Aisha Rahman: Yep and we need timeline expectations; our compliance window is tight, ISO evidence due mid-June.
[00:45] Priya Shah: Understood. We flagged three high/critical items in the report — CVE-2026-1234 (deserialization in a third-party lib), CVE-2026-1289 (priv escalation in infra agent), and a misconfig in SSO session settings that could allow long-lived tokens. There's also a medium finding around KV cache encryption — sometimes the notes say KV 'cash' in auto transcript, so ignore that.
[01:15] Tom Brooks: Wait, that infra agent — that runs on our Dedicated nodes in staging only currently. Production has managed agents but not installed this agent. Is it reproduced in prod?
[01:27] Priya Shah: From the test scope it looks like staging had the agent installed; production wasn't scanned for that specific vector, we recommend verifying. For the deserialization issue the vendor has a patch, we can advise patch order so you don't break dependencies.
[01:44] Jordan Park: On the audit log point Marcus raised — Redwood provides audit logs that capture token-level events and model routing decisions, but the exact retention depends on plan and can be exported to your S3 or SIEM. We'll include the export steps and a sample syslog config.
[02:02] Marcus Lee: Good — need to ensure logs are tamper-evident and hashed. Can we integrate with our KMS/HSM for log signing?
[02:10] Priya Shah: You can bring-your-own-KMS for encryption at rest; for signing we usually recommend shipping logs to your KMS-backed pipeline. We have customers who do HSM signing downstream. We'll capture recommended patterns in the doc.
[02:26] Aisha Rahman: On RBAC and SSO — the pen test flagged weak service account permissions that allowed escalation in the test env, and our SSO session length was long. We enforce 1-hour sessions normally. The screenshot in the report showed 24h.
[02:41] Tom Brooks: That 24h was an artifact from earlier onboarding; we intended to tighten it.
[02:45] Priya Shah: Ok that helps. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC; you can enforce session limits in the IdP. We'll include sample SAML attribute mappings and recommended RBAC roles for least privilege (Admin, Platform-Eng, Read-Only).
[03:05] Jordan Park: Can you quick share current patch cadence? Are you doing weekly patch windows?
[03:12] Tom Brooks: Weekly for infra images, but for app-level libs we rely on PRs and dependabot; we have a two-week sprint to apply critical patches but not formally guaranteed.
[03:22] Marcus Lee: That's the gap — for compliance we need guaranteed patch windows or documented compensating controls.
[03:27] Priya Shah: For the highest severity CVEs we recommend prioritizing kernel/agent patches first, then the library fixes. We'll propose a patch sequence that minimizes restarts for stateful services and provide a rollback plan.
[03:41] Aisha Rahman: Any specific guidance on CVE-2026-1234 — it's in a transitive dependency; patching might require upgrading the app's framework.
[03:49] Priya Shah: Right — for that one the options are: upgrade the consuming library which pulls the vulnerable transitive dep, or apply a runtime mitigation (like disabling the affected deserialization entry point). We can provide code snippets and test checklist.
[04:03] Jordan Park: Noted. On Dedicated vs Hosted — you mentioned Dedicated nodes earlier Tom, are you considering Redwood Dedicated or a private deployment?
[04:11] Tom Brooks: We're evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation. We might want Private if the auditors push for VPC-only control plane.
[04:19] Marcus Lee: For ISO and SOC2 evidence, we also need to know what is in-scope for Redwood-managed vs what we must own.
[04:26] Priya Shah: We'll send an evidence map — like who owns key rotation, where logs live, which controls Redwood attests to. For Private deployments you get more control and can integrate with your KMS/HSM directly. Dedicated still has isolation but control plane is managed.
[04:39] Aisha Rahman: On encryption — are server-side keys hardware-backed? We require HSM-backed KMS for production PII.
[04:46] Priya Shah: For Hosted we integrate with cloud KMS (customer-managed key supported). For Private we can support HSM options via your HSM provider. We'll note specific supported KMS providers.
[05:00] Jordan Park: Let's walk through the pen-test toplist. Priya, can you read the three criticals and suggested remediation order?
[05:06] Priya Shah: Sure — 1) CVE-2026-1289 infra agent priv esc — patch agent across staging first then prod, schedule agent upgrade during maintenance window; 2) CVE-2026-1234 deserialization — upgrade transitive dependency or apply runtime mitigation; 3) SSO session config — update IdP to enforce 1-hour sessions and rotate long-lived service tokens. Medium items: KV cache encryption observed as optional; recommend enabling encryption-in-transit and at-rest with customer KMS.
[05:36] Marcus Lee: For the agent patch we need an upgrade path that doesn't require full redeploy. Can Redwood provide a rolling upgrade script?
[05:42] Priya Shah: Yes we have documented rolling upgrade patterns for the infra agent; I'll share the script and a smoke-test checklist.
[05:49] Tom Brooks: Good. About regressions — we need an eval harness so upgrading libs doesn't break model outputs or latency.
[05:56] Jordan Park: Redwood Optimize can run quick regression checks; we'll include the evaluation harness template and guidance for Canary rollouts and A/B testing.
[06:09] Aisha Rahman: On vulnerability management — do you surface CVSS and exploitability? The pen test noted some 'high' items with CVSS 7.x but no exploit PoC.
[06:18] Priya Shah: We include CVSS scores in the report and tag findings with an exploitability likelihood when available. We'll recommend a triage rubric: Critical (CVSS 9-10 or active exploit), High (7-8.9), Medium (4-6.9). We'll also share a sample Jira template for tracking.
[06:35] Marcus Lee: Good. Any comments about rate-limiting or throttling in case of a DoS vector?
[06:41] Priya Shah: We have request-level throttles and routing policies; for public endpoints we recommend WAF and rate-limits at the edge plus autoscale policies to absorb bursts.
[06:51] Jordan Park: Switching to SDLC — secure coding checklist, SCA integration and pre-merge tests — what's your current pipeline?
[06:58] Tom Brooks: We run SCA (software composition analysis) on PRs via our CI, but it's not blocking. We also have unit tests; integration tests are flaky sometimes.
[07:09] Aisha Rahman: We want SCA to be blocking for high-severity vulnerabilities and to auto-open remediation PRs.
[07:16] Priya Shah: That's best practice; we can share recommended CI workflows, and a gating policy example where critical severity fails the build and creates a remediation ticket.
[07:27] Marcus Lee: Also need evidence for ISO — code review logs, SCA reports, and test run artifacts. Can Redwood provide templates for auditor packages?
[07:35] Priya Shah: Yes we'll provide an auditor evidence pack template and examples of what Redwood can attest to vs what you'd include.
[07:44] Tom Brooks: About patch cadence — if we commit to weekly infra and bi-weekly libs, what's Redwood's expectation for re-scans?
[07:53] Priya Shah: Re-scan after major patch windows is fine; for critical CVEs we recommend targeted re-scan within 48–72 hours of patching. We'll help run a focused scan and confirm closure.
[08:05] Marcus Lee: Can Redwood host a pen test in our staging after patches to validate?
[08:10] Jordan Park: We can coordinate a re-test with our partner testing team or you can run it with your provider; Redwood will help validate findings and help close the loop.
[08:19] Aisha Rahman: Any known regressions from the infra agent patch in other customers?
[08:24] Priya Shah: A few customers reported minor telemetry changes; nothing functional. We'll share rollback steps.
[08:31] Tom Brooks: OK. For the SSO token issue — can Redwood detect and alert for long-lived tokens?
[08:36] Priya Shah: We can add a detection rule in audit logs that flags tokens beyond threshold. We'll include example SIEM queries.
[08:44] Jordan Park: Action items recap — Priya will share remediation playbook and scripts; Jordan will send SOC2/ISO scope and pricing; Aisha to provide vuln tracker export; Tom to confirm patch cadence automation. Follow-up 2026-06-03.
[09:00] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. Minor note — there was a false positive in the pen test for a stale dependency report; we'll annotate that in the tracker.
[09:08] Priya Shah: Noted. We'll also include an approach for marking false positives and avoiding noisy alerts.
[09:15] Jordan Park: Anything else on compliance — SOC2 in particular? Marcus?
[09:19] Marcus Lee: We need the SOC2 in-scope list and evidence of encryption key rotation and access reviews for the last quarter.
[09:26] Priya Shah: We'll include key rotation logs and sample access review templates you can use. For Dedicated we can provide more granular logs on request.
[09:35] Aisha Rahman: One more — do you have guidance for embedding KMS calls in CI so that secrets never appear in build logs?
[09:40] Priya Shah: Yes recommend ephemeral credentials via short-lived tokens and KMS envelope encryption. We'll provide CI examples for GitHub Actions and Jenkins.
[09:50] Tom Brooks: Great. On timeline: we aim to close critical ones within 1 week, high within 2–3 weeks, and then run the re-scan. Is that realistic?
[09:58] Priya Shah: That's reasonable provided the upgrades don't require major app rewrites. We'll help triage which findings need code changes vs config/infra fixes.
[10:10] Jordan Park: Ok let's go through the documented next steps — we'll send the evidence pack, remediation playbook, rolling upgrade script, and pricing/options for Dedicated/Private.
[10:20] Marcus Lee: And we'll deliver the vuln tracker export and confirm patch windows.
[10:25] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and action items.

(occasional crosstalk, brief hold music in background when someone briefly dropped)

[54:30] Jordan Park: End recap — Priya: remediation docs and script by 2026-05-22; Jordan: SOC2/ISO evidence and pricing by 2026-05-25; Aisha: vuln tracker export by 2026-05-27; Tom: confirm automation & patch cadence by 2026-05-24. Next call 2026-06-03 to validate closures.
[54:52] Marcus Lee: Thanks all.
[54:55] Tom Brooks: Appreciate it.

Links referenced: pen-test-report.pdf (shared), SOC2-scope.xlsx (to be sent), rolling-upgrade-script.sh (will be shared), auditor-evidence-template.docx (will be shared).

End of transcript.
